docString:
Construct pointwise differentiated eigenbasis data from a simple finite spectrum.

The simple-spectrum hypothesis is expressed by injectivity of the band-energy map.
Energy derivatives are the lossless diagonal expectations of the self-adjoint Hamiltonian
derivatives. Eigenvector derivatives are constructed algebraically in the parallel-transport gauge
`⟪φ_n, ∂_μ φ_n⟫ = 0`, so a concrete model need not differentiate an explicit eigenvector gauge.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (hamiltonian : H →L[ℂ] H),
  IsSelfAdjoint hamiltonian →
    ∀ (eigenbasis : OrthonormalBasis ι ℂ H) (energy : ι → ℝ),
      (∀ (n : ι), hamiltonian (eigenbasis n) = ↑(energy n) • eigenbasis n) →
        ∀ (hamiltonianDerivative : κ → H →L[ℂ] H)
          (hamiltonianDerivative_selfAdjoint : ∀ (μ : κ), IsSelfAdjoint (hamiltonianDerivative μ)),
          Function.Injective energy →
            ∀ (μ : κ) (n : ι),
              (hamiltonianDerivative μ) (eigenbasis n) +
                  hamiltonian
                    (BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.simpleSpectrumEigenvectorDerivative✝ eigenbasis energy
                      hamiltonianDerivative μ n) =
                ↑((hamiltonianDerivative μ).diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (eigenbasis n)) • eigenbasis n +
                  ↑(energy n) •
                    BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.simpleSpectrumEigenvectorDerivative✝ eigenbasis energy
                      hamiltonianDerivative μ n
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.ofSimpleSpectrum._proof_1

  (∀ (μ : κ), IsSelfAdjoint (hamiltonianDerivative μ)) →
    Function.Injective energy →
      ∀ (μ : κ) (m n : ι),
        inner ℂ

                hamiltonianDerivative μ n) =

docString:
Shift an arbitrary differential functional from the source into the current without changing
what the balance law says.

For `K : OneForm' → Obs'`, this realizes

```text
J' = J + K,
S' = S - K ∘ d.
```

The subtraction is written as scalar multiplication by `-1`, so the construction only needs the
module structure on observables.

summable.

For the compact self-adjoint operators used by this project, this is the spectral summability
condition underlying spectral-trace arguments. The predicate itself deliberately does **not** assert
compactness or symmetry; those hypotheses are supplied separately wherever the spectral theorem is
used.

and the eigenvalue recorded at each index (`a.1.1`) depend only on the eigenspaces of `T` and their
dimensions, not on which orthonormal basis `stdOrthonormalBasis` happens to pick within each
(possibly multi-dimensional) eigenspace.

periodic configuration has order dividing one of `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, or `6`.

The determinant-one branch gives the crystallographic rotations; the determinant-minus-one
branch is an orientation-reversing orthogonal map and hence a reflection of order two.

must be the identity. This rules out nontrivial unipotent/shear matrices at the endpoint
of the crystallographic trace interval.

docString:
A unimodular integer matrix is realized as the integral-coordinate action
of an intrinsic lattice isometry if and only if it stabilizes the basis Gram
matrix. This gives the rank-independent classification criterion used to
identify symmetries of concrete Bravais metrics.

docString:
Among all integral bases of a discrete planar lattice, there is a basis
whose first vector has globally minimal norm. Its first vector is no longer
than its second vector, because swapping the vectors is again an integral
basis. This supplies the shortest-primitive-vector starting point for Gauss
basis reduction without assuming a preselected reduced basis.

    G 0 0 ≤ G 1 1 ∧ 2 * |G 0 1| ≤ G 0 0
name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.exists_gauss_reduced_basis
docString:
Every discrete rank-two integral lattice admits a Gauss-reduced primitive
basis. Its Gram matrix has nondecreasing diagonal coefficients and its
off-diagonal coefficient is at most half the first diagonal coefficient
in absolute value. The proof minimizes the first primitive basis vector
globally and then uses an integral shear, which keeps that vector fixed.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.exists_gram_integerShear_reduced
docString:
Every positive planar first Gram coefficient admits an integer shear
that reduces the off-diagonal entry to at most half of that coefficient in
absolute value. This is the size-reduction step of Gauss lattice reduction;
it does not yet assert the ordering of the two diagonal coefficients.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.exists_gram_swapShear_descends
docString:
If the second primitive vector is shorter than the first, swapping the
vectors and size-reducing by an integer shear gives a new primitive basis
whose first squared length strictly decreases and whose off-diagonal Gram
coefficient is at most half that first squared length.

This is the descent step of the Gauss algorithm. Termination requires an
additional discreteness argument for the squared lengths of lattice vectors.

exactly when they have equal squared lengths. This is the rhombic primitive-basis
condition relevant to the centered-rectangular Bravais class. It is not by
itself an exhaustive characterization of that class.

docString:

in every integral lattice basis. Each column of the integral matrix contains
the basis coordinates of an image basis vector. The result is rank-generic and
independent of any atomic motif.

change of coordinates. In a lattice basis change the matrices `P` and `Q`
have integral entries and satisfy `Q = P⁻¹`; the statement only uses their
real inverse relations. The symmetry matrix changes by conjugation, while
the Gram matrix changes by congruence.

rotation forces an equilateral primitive basis: equal squared lengths and
twice the off-diagonal inner product equal to their common squared length.

orthogonality of this conventional cell forces that edge condition.
Unlike an integral primitive basis change, this matrix has determinant `2`.

integer matrices preserves the metric if and only if its two diagonal entries
agree and the absolute off-diagonal entry is half their common value.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.gram_standard_reflection_walls_iff
docString:
Three explicitly exhibited kinds of integral reflection witness pick out
the three walls of the planar Gauss-reduced metric region: an orthogonal
primitive basis, equal primitive lengths, or the size-reduction edge.

The result classifies these *standard witnesses*, not all possible reflection
matrices up to integral conjugacy. That completeness statement requires an
additional arithmetic argument.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.gram_sumDiff_diagonal_iff
docString:
The sum and difference of two primitive lattice vectors form an orthogonal
conventional cell exactly when the vectors have equal squared lengths.

For a symmetric Gram metric `G`, the columns of `S = !![1, 1; 1, -1]`
are the sum and difference of the primitive basis vectors. When `G₀₀ = G₁₁`,
the conventional squared lengths are `2 * (G₀₀ + G₀₁)` and
`2 * (G₀₀ - G₀₁)`. This is the metric relation underlying the
centered-rectangular Bravais class. The matrix `S` has determinant `-2`,
so this conventional cell is not an integral primitive basis change.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.integerShear_det
docString: An integer shear of a planar primitive basis is unimodular.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.integerSwapShear_det
docString:
Swapping the planar basis vectors and then applying an integer shear
is an integral primitive basis change of determinant minus one.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.integer_fixedFirst_reflection_normalform
docString:
An integral matrix of determinant minus one fixing the first
primitive basis vector is necessarily a shear-reflection. No metric
hypothesis is needed for this arithmetic normal form.

name: LeanCondensedMatter.Crystal.latticePointGroup.integer_fixedFirst_reflection_parity_normalform
docString:
Every integer reflection fixing the first vector is shear-conjugate
to one with coefficient zero or one. Thus the integer conjugacy class
depends only on the shear coefficient modulo two.

A row-and-column locally finite hopping model on an arbitrary discrete site type.

`column y` is the finitely supported vector `h |y⟩`. The finite set `incident x` contains `x` and

name: LocallyFiniteHopping.oneParticleBondContact
docString:
The first source derivative of the Peierls current. Both hopping orientations carry the
coefficient `-(i q / ℏ)²`; it is kept in factorized form to match the derivative construction.

statement:
∀ {Site : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq Site] (K : LocallyFiniteHopping Site) (ℏ q : ℂ) (x y : Site),
  K.oneParticleBondContact ℏ q x y =
    (QuantumTheory.PeierlsPhase.peierlsCoupling ℏ q * -QuantumTheory.PeierlsPhase.peierlsCoupling ℏ q) •
        K.amplitude x y • matrixUnit x y +
      (-QuantumTheory.PeierlsPhase.peierlsCoupling ℏ q * QuantumTheory.PeierlsPhase.peierlsCoupling ℏ q) •
        K.amplitude y x • matrixUnit y x
name: LocallyFiniteHopping.oneParticleBondContact.eq_1

conclusion.text:

docString:
The two oriented hopping terms on a link with opposite Peierls phases.

This is the link contribution, not the full hopping Hamiltonian. Link variables remain separate
from a uniform vector potential. Geometric link coordinates and their finite-lattice aggregation
are owned by `Lattice.GeometricCurrent` and `Lattice.GeometricPeierls`; response and conductivity
specializations remain downstream in `Fermionic.Transport`.

    QuantumTheory.PeierlsPhase.peierlsForwardPhase ℏ q A • K.amplitude x y • matrixUnit x y +

name: QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.finiteDimensional_schrodinger_continuity
docString:
Pointwise finite-dimensional continuity equation assembled from coordinate-line derivatives.

For each coordinate `i`, `ψSpace i` is the restriction of the wavefunction to the coordinate line
through the selected spatial point, and `ψx i` is its first spatial derivative along that line.
The family `secondDerivatives` contains the diagonal second derivatives at the point. The conclusion
is the coordinate expression

`∂ₜρ + ∑ i, ∂ᵢjᵢ = 0`.

docString:
The scalar-potential Schrödinger equation gives the time derivative of the spatially smeared
probability density.

The conclusion is

`d/dt ∫ test * ρ = ∫ test' * j - (test(b)j(b) - test(a)j(a))`.

Time differentiation under the integral uses the explicit dominated-derivative hypotheses above;
the spatial current term is supplied by the previously proved interval weak continuity theorem.

name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel
docString:
Neutral data specifying one bounded linear-response channel.

`measured` is the source-independent zeroth-order measured observable, `source` is the operator
coupled to the scalar source, and `observableVariation` is the first-order variation of the
measured observable itself.  The latter is kept explicit so contact terms are not silently dropped
when generalized currents depend on the external source.

name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel.causalResponse
docString:
Causal scalar response of a channel to a real source profile.

The first term is the ordinary retarded Kubo response and the second is the explicit observable
variation/contact contribution. The profile is not applied again to the supplied variation.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (channel : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel H) (U : Multiplicative ℝ →* ↥(unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))) (hbar : ℝ)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ),
  channel.causalResponse U hbar expectation f t =
    (∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t, ↑(f s) * channel.retardedKernel U hbar expectation t s) +
      channel.contactExpectation U expectation t

name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel.finiteTimeAdiabaticResponse
docString:
Finite-observation-time adiabatic response of a neutral response channel.

The source value at the observation time has been factored out, so the retarded kernel carries the
lag phase `exp ((i ω - η) (T - s))` while the explicit observable variation contributes its
contact expectation at `T`. No stationarity or infinite-time limit is assumed.

statement: ∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H], ContinuousAdd H
name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel.finiteTimeAdiabaticResponse._proof_1

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (channel : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel H) (U : Multiplicative ℝ →* ↥(unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))) (hbar : ℝ)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (ω η T : ℝ),
  channel.finiteTimeAdiabaticResponse U hbar expectation ω η T =
    (∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..T,
        QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticFrequencyPhase ω η (T - s) *
          channel.retardedKernel U hbar expectation T s) +
      channel.contactExpectation U expectation T
name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.ResponseChannel.finiteTimeAdiabaticResponse.eq_1

conclusion.text:
channel.finiteTimeAdiabaticResponse U hbar expectation ω η T =
  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.finiteTimeAdiabaticTransform
      (fun τ =>
        QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.commutatorSusceptibility U hbar expectation channel.measured channel.source τ 0)
      ω η T +
    expectation.toContinuousLinearMap channel.observableVariation

the Bloch relation twice.

conclusion.text:
QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params energy =
  Real.cos (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy * params.barrierWidth) *
      Real.cos (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth) -
    (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy /
              QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy +
            QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy /
              QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy) /
          2 *
        Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy * params.barrierWidth) *
      Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth)

                      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy +

                      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy) /

              Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth)

dispersion formula rather than an artifact of totalized division.

docString:
The finite-cutoff Born-Dyson single-pole radial integral is exactly
a difference of principal complex logarithms whenever the real part of
its effective spectral center is positive. Finite-`η` invertibility
excludes all real momentum poles and supplies the required nonzero
imaginary part of that center; no additional log-branch assumption is made.
This is before broadening and disorder limits.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonAngularGreenEntryKernel
docString:
Finite-cutoff angular Green entry kernel at an arbitrary polar real-space point.
The constant Pauli channels carry `K0`; the in-plane Pauli vector rotates as
`(cos angle, sin angle)` in the first Fourier harmonic `K1`. The physical
momentum measure is attached by the Fourier integral, not by this kernel.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide)
  (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius angle p : ℝ) (i j : Fin 2),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonAngularGreenEntryKernel side v m probeEnergy
      broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius angle p i j =
    ↑p *
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient side v m p 0 probeEnergy
                  broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax •
                1 +
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
                  side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax •
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ)
            i j +
        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
          (↑(Real.cos angle) *
              (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax •
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX)
                i j +
            ↑(Real.sin angle) *
              (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax •
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY)
                i j))
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonAngularGreenEntryKernel.eq_1

conclusion.text:
have a :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening
    disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have b :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x side v m p
    0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have d :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z side v m p
    0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have k0 := QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar);
have k1 := QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar);
(fun i j =>
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonAngularGreenEntryKernel side v m probeEnergy
      broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius angle p i j) =
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneSpinRotation angle *
      ↑p • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.polarPauliMatrix (k0 * a) (k1 * b) (k0 * d) 0 *
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneSpinRotationInverse angle

conductivity contribution.

The two crossed current blocks are built from dimensionless Pauli current vertices upstream, so the
physical current scale contributes `(e v)²`. Their Fourier transforms already contain the physical
momentum measure, hence only `bastinStredaTraceConductivityPrefactor` is attached here.

The two leading crossed topologies remain indexed upstream, but their physical response is exposed
through one additive boundary here. This keeps the `X` / `Psi` decomposition available for later
evaluation while giving downstream Hall consumers one object for the complete Gaussian crossed
correction. No crossed topology is absorbed into the non-crossing ladder by this definition.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedOrderedXYConductivity_eq_radial_antisymmetric_trace
docString:
The physically normalized crossed Hall contribution reduces to the radial
antisymmetric source-pair trace at finite momentum and real-space cutoffs.
The existing Fourier measures remain inside the radial trace tensor, while
the two disorder correlators and the trace-only Bastin prefactor occur once.
This does not evaluate the radial integral or assert a regulator limit.

conclusion.text:
QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedOrderedXYConductivity
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.psi e v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
    rMax =
  ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.bastinStredaTraceConductivityPrefactor hbar * (e * v) ^ 2) * ↑(disorderStrength ^ 2) *
      ↑(2 * Real.pi) *
    ∫ (radius : ℝ) in 0..rMax,
      ↑radius *
        have factor :=
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedCurrentFactor v m probeEnergy
            broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have aA := fun p =>
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have aR := fun p =>
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have dA := fun p =>
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have dR := fun p =>
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have bA := fun p =>
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have bR := fun p =>
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
        have isotropic :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              2 * ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  ((aA p * aR p - dA p * dR p) * factor));
        have anisotropic :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              2 * ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  (bA p * bR p * factor));
        have firstX :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  ((aR p * bA p + aA p * bR p) * factor));
        have firstY :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  (-Complex.I * (bR p * dA p - bA p * dR p) * factor));
        have greenFirst := Complex.I * ↑(radius / hbar) / 2;
        have greenSecondMoment :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              ↑p ^ 2 *
                ((QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) -
                    QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) *
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy
                    broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax);
        have greenScalar :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient
                    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar
                    pMax);
        have greenZ :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy
                    broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax);
        have transverse :=
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              ↑p *
                (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                  (Complex.I * (aR p * dA p - aA p * dR p) * factor));
        have minor :=
          greenFirst * greenSecondMoment * (firstX * ((isotropic - anisotropic) / 2) - firstY * transverse) -
            greenScalar * (transverse ^ 2 + (isotropic ^ 2 - anisotropic ^ 2) / 4);
        ↑(-8 * (greenZ.re * minor.im + greenZ.im * minor.re))

docString:
The finite-regulator physical Psi Hall integrand now contains only explicit
K0/K1/K2 radial momentum moments: the remaining retarded Green scalar/z
coefficients and source-x transverse current coefficient are expanded as well.
Each Fourier block retains its existing momentum measure. This is an exact
reduction, not a real-space radial evaluation or any regulator limit.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedOrderedXYConductivity_psi_eq_real_minor_radial_integral
docString:
The physically normalized regulated Psi crossed Hall conductivity is
the radial integral of a *real-valued* minor kernel. In contrast to the
conjugate-symmetrized amplitude representation, the integrand uses only
the real and imaginary parts of two independent scalar products.
No cancellation, radial integration, or cutoff/broadening limit is asserted.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedOrderedXYConductivity_psi_eq_transverse_radial_integral
docString:
The regulated physical Psi Hall contribution is the finite-radius integral
of its transverse-current-reduced antisymmetric Pauli amplitude and its
complex-conjugate partner. This is a substitution into the canonical
diagram-indexed conductivity boundary, not a claim of Psi cancellation or
of convergence after removing either cutoff.

      greenFirst *

      greenFirst * (greenScalarA * greenSecondMoment greenBR - greenScalarR * greenSecondMoment greenBA);

            ((isotropic ^ 2 - anisotropic ^ 2) / 4 + transverseX ^ 2) +
        greenScalarX * (first * (diagonalY * zX - transverseX * zY)))

docString:
The regulated physical X Hall radial integrand is expressed solely in the
canonical K0/K1/K2 momentum moments, with the remaining retarded/advanced
Green scalar and z coefficients, transverse source-x current, and diagonal
source-y current all expanded. The signed Green radius and one Fourier
measure per real-space block remain explicit. No real-space integration or
regulator limit is asserted.

  broadening ≠ 0 →

        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedOrderedXYConductivity

            hbar pMax rMax =
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.bastinStredaTraceConductivityPrefactor hbar * (e * v) ^ 2) *
                ↑(disorderStrength ^ 2) *
              ↑(2 * Real.pi) *
            ∫ (radius : ℝ) in 0..rMax,
              ↑radius *
                have Jx :=
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialRealSpaceCurrentBlock
                    0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
                have Jy :=
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialRealSpaceCurrentBlock
                    1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
                have GR :=
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix
                    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
                    (-radius);
                have GA :=
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix
                    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
                    (-radius);
                have a := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient Jx;
                have b := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient GR;
                have c := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient Jy;
                have d := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient GA;
                have u := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient Jx;
                have vr := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient GR;
                have w := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient Jy;
                have va := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient GA;
                2 * Complex.I *
                  ((a * w InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y - c * u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y) *
                        (vr InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x * va InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z -
                          vr InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z * va InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x) +
                      (b * va InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z - d * vr InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z) *
                        (w InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y * u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x + u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y ^ 2) +
                    (d * vr InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x - b * va InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x) *

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient_diagonal_ra_denominator_harmonics
docString:
The two independent diagonal Gaussian-crossed current harmonics have a
single finite-broadening RA Dyson denominator. Their K0 numerator is the
effective-energy product minus the effective-mass product, while the K2
numerator is the squared in-plane Dirac momentum. The Fourier momentum
measure and disorder/current factor are unchanged. No denominator is
assumed nonzero and no regulator limit is taken.

conclusion.text:

  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;

    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have massR :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded
    v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have massA :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced
    v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have factor :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedCurrentFactor v m probeEnergy
    broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
have gap := energyA ^ 2 - massA ^ 2 - (energyR ^ 2 - massR ^ 2);
have jxx :=
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;

    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;

  2 * ↑p * QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *

  2 * ↑p * QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * (↑(v * p) ^ 2 * factor);

At zero real-space separation, the isotropic Gaussian-crossed current
is an exactly evaluated finite-cutoff RA radial moment. Both diagonal
Pauli coefficients agree by rotational symmetry. The original physical
Fourier measure occurs only once, and the RA spectral-center gap is
retained on the left rather than inverted. The complex logarithms use
the finite-broadening Dyson branch criterion. Neither a nonzero-radius
K0/K2 moment nor a complete X/Psi Hall diagram is evaluated here.

  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliKernel

                    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar
                    pMax *
                  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient
                    QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar
                    pMax -
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy
                    broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax *

                    InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy
                    broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax) *
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedCurrentFactor v m
                probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax) +
          QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
            (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x

                probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax))

docString:
The diagonal in-plane crossed-current Pauli kernels separate into a rotationally
isotropic zeroth harmonic and a traceless second harmonic. Their sum removes `K2` and
their difference removes `K0`, before taking any momentum or real-space integral.

This is a finite-cutoff pointwise identity; it neither assumes nor proves convergence of
a regulator limit.

docString:
The four non-diagonal first-harmonic channels of the regulated Gaussian-crossed
radial current are exact source-resolved scalar momentum integrals. The source-x and
source-y Pauli-scalar and Pauli-z components all use the same Fourier K1 kernel,
with distinct spectral coefficient combinations and signs.

These finite-cutoff identities reuse the physical Fourier momentum measure and do
not evaluate the radial integrals or remove the regulators.

The zeroth-radius crossed-current block has neither a Pauli-scalar nor a
longitudinal Pauli-z component. Both channels carry the first angular Fourier
harmonic, which vanishes at the origin before momentum integration.

This is an exact finite-broadening, finite-cutoff selection rule; it does not
require a real-space regulator limit.

    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient

                    ((QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) -
                        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) *
                      (-Complex.I * (bR p * dA p - bA p * dR p) * factor)));
          have d :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                ↑p * (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * aA p);
          have isotropic :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                2 * ↑p *
                  (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                    ((aA p * aR p - dA p * dR p) * factor));
          have anisotropic :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                2 * ↑p *
                  (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                    (bA p * bR p * factor));
          have ux := (isotropic + anisotropic) / 2;
          have uy :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                ↑p *
                  (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                    (Complex.I * (aR p * dA p - aA p * dR p) * factor));
          have uz :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              (Complex.I * ↑(radius / hbar) / 2 *
                ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                  ↑p ^ 2 *
                    ((QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) -
                        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) *
                      ((bR p * dA p + bA p * dR p) * factor)));
          have wx := -uy;
          have wy := (isotropic - anisotropic) / 2;
          have wz :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              (Complex.I * ↑(radius / hbar) / 2 *
                ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                  ↑p ^ 2 *
                    ((QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) -
                        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) *
                      (-Complex.I * (aA p * bR p - aR p * bA p) * factor)));
          have grx :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              (Complex.I * ↑(radius / hbar) / 2 *
                ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                  ↑p ^ 2 *
                    ((QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) -
                        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) *
                      bR p));
          have grz :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                ↑p * (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * dR p);
          have gax :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              (Complex.I * ↑(radius / hbar) / 2 *
                ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                  ↑p ^ 2 *
                    ((QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) -
                        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) *
                      bA p));
          have gaz :=
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                ↑p * (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * dA p);
          2 *
            ((a * b - ux * grx + uz * grz) * (c * d - wx * gax + wz * gaz) +
                  (-a * grx + b * ux + Complex.I * uy * grz) * (-c * gax + d * wx + Complex.I * wy * gaz) +
                (b * uy - Complex.I * (uz * grx + ux * grz)) * (d * wy - Complex.I * (wz * gax + wx * gaz)) +
              (a * grz + b * uz + Complex.I * uy * grx) * (c * gaz + d * wz + Complex.I * wy * gax))

  ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
    ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
      ↑p *

          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z

have greenZA :=
  ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
    ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,

        (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * -radius / hbar) *

    ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,

        have Jy :=
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialRealSpaceCurrentBlock 1 v
            m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
        have GR :=
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
            (-radius);
        have GA :=
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
            (-radius);
        have a := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient Jx;
        have b := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient GR;
        have c := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient Jy;
        have d := InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient GA;
        have u := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient Jx;
        have vr := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient GR;
        have w := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient Jy;
        have va := InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient GA;
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialTraceTensor
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.x v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength
              hbar pMax radius 0 1 -

              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.x v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength

              (d * vr InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x - b * va InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x) *

its canonical radial source-pair trace tensor under SO(2), the *complete*
finite-radius real-space integral is the radial integral of the antisymmetric

the model's Green/current rotation laws. This theorem performs the angular
projection, not the remaining radial or regulator limits.

statement:
∀ (e v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonLongitudinalRetardedAdvancedDressedSurfaceMomentumIntegralZeroBroadeningBoundary
      e v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax =
    2 * (↑(-e) * ↑v) ^ 2 *
          (↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDisorderMeasurePrefactor disorderStrength hbar))⁻¹ *
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneLadderAction
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonCurrentRungVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary v m
            probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax)
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonLadderSolvedVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary v m
            probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax)
          0 -
      ↑(2 * Real.pi) * (↑(-e) * ↑v) ^ 2 *
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroBroadeningSameSideRadialEndpoint
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax +
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroBroadeningSameSideRadialEndpoint
            QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax)

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel
docString:
Scalar radial momentum kernel for one finite-cutoff Born-Dyson Green-matrix entry. The
physical momentum-measure prefactor remains outside the one-dimensional integral.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p : ℝ)
  (i j : Fin 2),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m probeEnergy broadening
      disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p i j =
    ↑p *
      !![QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient side v m p 0
                  probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax +
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                  InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax),
            QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x
                side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
          QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x
                side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax,
            QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient side v m p 0
                  probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax -
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                  InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)]
        i j
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel.eq_1

docString:
The retarded/advanced Green transverse minor in the physical X Hall
amplitude has only K0 and K2 momentum moments. The first-harmonic
in-plane components share the explicit factor `i * (radius / hbar) / 2`,
which is factored out before the remaining real-space radius integral.

This identity keeps the physical Fourier momentum measure in *each* Green
block. It makes no assumption about the sign of `radius`, removes no
regulator, and does not evaluate the remaining radial integral.

docString:
The finite-broadening retarded and advanced massive-Dirac Dyson spectral
centers are distinct in the metallic-center region. The real part of the
retarded center is positive, so if its imaginary part vanished there would
be a pole at real momentum. Dyson invertibility excludes that pole; spectral
conjugation then makes the advanced-minus-retarded center gap nonzero.
No zero-broadening, disorder, or cutoff limit is taken.

docString:
At finite broadening and cutoff, the unweighted RA radial double-pole
moment reduces to logarithmic boundary values of the retarded and advanced
Dyson denominators. The spectral-center gap multiplies the moment, so the
identity does not silently assume that the gap is invertible. Positive real
parts of both spectral centers ensure the log-branch hypotheses by finite-η
Dyson invertibility. This is a radial building block, not an evaluation
of the nonzero-radius K0/K2 Fourier moments or an X/Psi conductivity.

    0 0 e v m p probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax =
  have q := ↑(-e) * ↑v;
  have solved :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedDressedSourceCurrentCoefficientVector
      0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
  have eR :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
      QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
  have massR :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
      QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
  have dR :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator
      QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
  have eA :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
      QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
  have massA :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
      QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
  have dA :=
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator
      QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel
docString:
Pointwise trace kernel for the two leading crossed Gaussian Hall topologies.

The separation type is required only to support `r ↦ -r`, allowing the same topology to be reused
for Cartesian real-space vectors and scalar radial coordinates.

The `realSpaceCurrentBlock` argument is Ado's `J_r` block from Eq. (14), not the local dressed vertex
`Γ`. For `x` this is
`Tr(Jˣ(r) Gᴿ(-r) Jʸ(r) Gᴬ(-r))`.

For `psi` the traced amplitude is
`Tr(Jˣ(r) Gᴿ(-r) Gᴿ(r) Jʸ(-r)) + h.c.`;
the Hermitian-conjugate contribution is represented after taking the trace as complex conjugation.

statement: NeZero (1 + 1)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel._proof_1

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Neg R] (greenRetarded greenAdvanced : R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2)
  (realSpaceCurrentBlock : Fin 2 → R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (r : R),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.x greenRetarded greenAdvanced realSpaceCurrentBlock r =
    (realSpaceCurrentBlock 0 r * greenRetarded (-r) * realSpaceCurrentBlock 1 r * greenAdvanced (-r)).trace
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel.eq_1

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Neg R] (greenRetarded greenAdvanced : R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2)
  (realSpaceCurrentBlock : Fin 2 → R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (r : R),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.psi greenRetarded greenAdvanced realSpaceCurrentBlock r =
    (realSpaceCurrentBlock 0 r * greenRetarded (-r) * greenRetarded r * realSpaceCurrentBlock 1 (-r)).trace +
      (starRingEnd ℂ)
        (realSpaceCurrentBlock 0 r * greenRetarded (-r) * greenRetarded r * realSpaceCurrentBlock 1 (-r)).trace

docString:
Exact finite-cutoff radial primitive for a massive-Dirac propagator with
arbitrary complex effective energy and mass. The nonzero imaginary part of
the squared-energy-minus-mass center keeps the whole radial path off the
principal logarithm's branch cut. This extends the clean-regulator Born
primitive to the complex Dyson parameters used by crossed RA diagrams,
without taking any disorder, broadening, or cutoff limit.

statement:
∀ (μ ν : Fin 2) (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py probeEnergy broadening : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.interbandSpectatorCurrentFactor μ ν band e v m px py probeEnergy broadening =
    QuantumTheory.Transport.scalarResolventCoefficient
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.retardedSpectralParameter probeEnergy broadening)
            (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandEnergy (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) v m px
              py) ^
          2 *
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.currentBandBlockTrace μ ν
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) band e v m px py -
      QuantumTheory.Transport.scalarResolventCoefficient
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.advancedSpectralParameter probeEnergy broadening)
            (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandEnergy (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) v m px
              py) ^
          2 *
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.currentBandBlockTrace ν μ
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) band e v m px py

docString:

Eq. (12a) plus side-jump Eq. (12b) plus full skew Eq. (18) sum.

This combines algebraic benchmark identities, not the unproved
regulated-X/Psi-integral evaluation or an independent microscopic

conclusion.text:

  -(e ^ 2 / QuantumTheory.planckConstantFromReduced hbar) *
    (2 * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (probeEnergy * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2)));
have nonCrossingSkewType :=
  -(e ^ 2 / QuantumTheory.planckConstantFromReduced hbar) *
    (3 * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) ^ 2 / (2 * probeEnergy * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2) ^ 2));
QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.intrinsicHallConductivity e hbar m probeEnergy + sideJumpType + nonCrossingSkewType =
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.nonCrossingHallConductivity e hbar m probeEnergy

      have nonCrossingSkewType :=
        -(e ^ 2 / QuantumTheory.planckConstantFromReduced hbar) *

        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.nonCrossingHallConductivity e hbar m probeEnergy

correction on the left is the required sum of those contributions after taking those limits.

integral with this expression.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.orderedXYRungSolvedProvenanceConductivityLimit_eq_intrinsic_sideJumpType_nonCrossingSkewType_partition
docString:
The physically normalized concrete provenance vector partitions the Ado Eq. (12) mechanisms
from I. A. Ado et al., *EPL* **111**, 37004 (2015),
[doi:10.1209/0295-5075/111/37004](https://doi.org/10.1209/0295-5075/111/37004).
The paper's Eqs. (12a-c) are the intrinsic, side-jump, and non-crossing-skew components; the
theorem below algebraically partitions the weak-disorder limit of the ordered finite-cutoff
ladder provenance. This does not derive separate microscopic side-jump collision or
skew-scattering kernels.
The side-jump-type term is shared between the two provenance components rather than attached to only
one of them. The `sideJumpType` and `nonCrossingSkewType` names are local to this theorem statement and
do not create primitive mechanism APIs.

  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.polarPauliInPlaneHarmonics aL bL dL aR bR dR coefficients =
    {
      constant :=
        ((aL * aR - dL * dR) * coefficients 0 - Complex.I * (aR * dL - aL * dR) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX +
          (Complex.I * (aR * dL - aL * dR) * coefficients 0 + (aL * aR - dL * dR) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY,
      firstCosine :=
        ((aR * bL + aL * bR) * coefficients 0 - Complex.I * (bR * dL - bL * dR) * coefficients 1) • 1 +
          ((bR * dL + bL * dR) * coefficients 0 - Complex.I * (aL * bR - aR * bL) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ,
      firstSine :=
        (Complex.I * (bR * dL - bL * dR) * coefficients 0 + (aR * bL + aL * bR) * coefficients 1) • 1 +
          (Complex.I * (aL * bR - aR * bL) * coefficients 0 + (bR * dL + bL * dR) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ,
      secondCosine :=
        (bL * bR * coefficients 0) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX -
          (bL * bR * coefficients 1) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY,
      secondMixed :=
        (2 * bL * bR * coefficients 1) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX +
          (2 * bL * bR * coefficients 0) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY }

to its zero-broadening boundary.

  (fun disorderStrength =>
    have q := ↑(-e) * ↑v;
    have pref := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDisorderMeasurePrefactor disorderStrength hbar);
    have solved :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonLadderSolvedVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary v m
        probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have rung :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonCurrentRungVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary v m
        probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have normalization := ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.bastinStredaPhysicalMomentumConductivityNormalization hbar);
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
      (normalization * (-2 * q ^ 2 * pref⁻¹ * (rung 1 * solved 0)))
      (normalization * (-2 * q ^ 2 * pref⁻¹ * (rung 0 * solved 1))))

docString:
Upper-band Fermi-surface density-of-states factor from the isotropic radial Jacobian in the
physical-momentum measure `d²p/(2πℏ)²`.

The definition is total as a real-valued expression.  Its density-of-states interpretation and
closed form below use the strict metallic regime, where the Fermi circle and radial derivative are
nonzero.

statement: (1 + 1).AtLeastTwo

conclusion.text:

  fermiEnergy / (2 * Real.pi * hbar ^ 2 * v ^ 2)

          fermiEnergy / (2 * Real.pi * hbar ^ 2 * v ^ 2)

docString:
In the strict metallic regime `|m| < ε_F`, the Fermi-circle Jacobian gives the single-cone
upper-band DOS

`D_F = ε_F / (2π ℏ² v²)`.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity
docString:
Zero-temperature Fermi-surface relaxation-time-approximation benchmark for the longitudinal
electrical conductivity.

The supplied `transportLifetime` is `τ_tr`, a positive current-relaxation time assumed uniform around
the isotropic Fermi circle, which is why it multiplies the angularly averaged `v_x²` as one scalar.
This definition does not claim that `τ_tr` follows from the clean Hamiltonian or from a self-energy
broadening.

conclusion.text:
QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity e hbar v m fermiEnergy
    (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornUpperBandPositiveTransportLifetime v m fermiEnergy disorderStrength
      hbar hvelocity hhbar hdisorder hmF) =
  e ^ 2 * hbar * v ^ 2 * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (Real.pi * disorderStrength * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2))

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity_bornTransportLifetime_eq
docString:
The zero-temperature massive-Dirac RTA benchmark evaluated on the microscopic Born transport
lifetime has the explicit `1/W` form

`σxx = e² ℏ v² (εF² - m²) / [π W (εF² + 3 m²)]`.

The positivity assumptions are exactly those used to package the microscopic lifetime as a
`PositiveTransportLifetime`; no finite clean-disorder limit is asserted.

statement:
∀ (c₁ c₂ : ℝ) (k : Fin 3 → ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalZDoubleCommutator c₁ c₂ k =
    -((QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalHamiltonian c₁ c₂ k *
                (QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalHamiltonian c₁ c₂ k *
                    QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.generatorZ -
                  QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.generatorZ *
                    QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalHamiltonian c₁ c₂ k) -
              (QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalHamiltonian c₁ c₂ k *
                    QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.generatorZ -
                  QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.generatorZ *
                    QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalHamiltonian c₁ c₂ k) *
                QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.orbitalHamiltonian c₁ c₂ k) *
            QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.generatorZ).trace /
      2

      QuantumTheory.Models.OrbitalRelaxation.momentumOuter k +

statement:

  Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℝ → QuantumTheory.Transport.AngularHarmonicCoefficients ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients
docString:
Canonical constant/second-harmonic representation of the product of two Cartesian current
components on a circle of radius `p`.

For equal directions the constant piece is one half of `(q p / m_eff)²`; the second-cosine
coefficient distinguishes `xx` from `yy`. For unequal directions the product is purely the mixed
second harmonic. The common current scale is obtained from `currentComponent`.

statement: (1 + 1).AtLeastTwo
name: QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients._proof_1

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.Parameters) (measured source : Fin 2) (p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients params measured source p =
    if _hEq : measured = source then
      if _hX : measured = 0 then
        { constant := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2, firstCosine := 0,
          firstSine := 0, secondCosine := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2,
          secondMixed := 0 }
      else
        { constant := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2, firstCosine := 0,
          firstSine := 0, secondCosine := -(↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2),
          secondMixed := 0 }
    else
      { constant := 0, firstCosine := 0, firstSine := 0, secondCosine := 0,
        secondMixed := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) }
name: QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients.eq_1

`Ω_b = -s_b Δ α_R² / (2 |d|³)`.

    (QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.currentBoundedOperator params measured px py)
    (QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.currentBoundedOperator params source px py) params.chemicalPotential
    params.broadening

            ensemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded)
              (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced))),
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameter QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced energy broadening -
            QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameter QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded energy broadening) •
          (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded *
              QuantumTheory.Transport.resummedLadderVertex
                (ensemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded)
                  (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced))
                hinvertible charge *
            solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced) =
        solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded * charge -
          charge * solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.FiniteSCBASolution.resummedLadderVertex_charge_ward_consistency
docString:
Finite SCBA/RA charge-vertex Ward consistency. Under the minimal charge-symmetry interface and
the same conditional ladder invertibility used by the generic resummation, the generic corrected
charge vertex `Γ_Q = (I - L_RA)⁻¹ Q` obeys

`(zᴬ - zᴿ) • (Ḡᴿ Γ_Q Ḡᴬ) = Ḡᴿ Q - Q Ḡᴬ`.

For `Q = 1`, the right-hand side is `Ḡᴿ - Ḡᴬ`.

  charge *
            (algebraMap ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H))
              (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameter QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced energy

    charge *

                broadening) +

                (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameter QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded energy

    freeGreen * freeInverse = 1 →

        dressedGreen * dressedInverse = 1 →
          (QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy ↔
            selfEnergy = freeInverse - dressedInverse)

The supplied identity needed to cancel the observable variation and static normalization.
In a Peierls model its proof is a model-specific Ward/f-sum problem.

docString:
Finite-band clean Bloch data with an explicitly supplied occupied spectral projector.

The projector is characterized without a global eigenvector gauge: on every Hamiltonian
eigenvector it acts as the identity below the Fermi level and as zero above it. The separate
Fermi-gap field excludes the boundary case. This is the first vertical-slice boundary; constructing
the projector from functional calculus can be added later without changing downstream topology.

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteCutoffPhysicalMomentumPolarFourier
docString:
Finite-cutoff polar Fourier transform of a complex scalar momentum field with the physical
momentum measure `d²p / (2πℏ)²` included exactly once.

conclusion.text:
QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteCutoffPhysicalMomentumPolarFourier hbar pMax (fun p θ => (coefficients p).eval θ)
    (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarPoint2D radius angle) =
  ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
    ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
      ↑p *
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * (coefficients p).constant +
            QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              (↑(Real.cos angle) * (coefficients p).firstCosine + ↑(Real.sin angle) * (coefficients p).firstSine) +
          QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
            ((↑(Real.cos angle) ^ 2 - ↑(Real.sin angle) ^ 2) * (coefficients p).secondCosine +
              ↑(Real.cos angle) * ↑(Real.sin angle) * (coefficients p).secondMixed))

`J0 + J2 = 2 J1/z` recurrence, stated without division by `z`.

∀ {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype ι] (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.EnergyEigenbasisLehmannData system ι) (current₁ current₂ : H →L[ℂ] H)
  (energy broadening : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinSpectralTraceSum system data current₁ current₂ energy broadening =
    ∑ m,
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded energy
            broadening m -
          QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced energy
            broadening m) *
        (∑ n,
            QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded
                    energy broadening n ^
                  2 *
                inner ℂ (data.basis m) (current₁ (data.basis n)) *
              inner ℂ (data.basis n) (current₂ (data.basis m)) -
          ∑ n,
            QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced
                    energy broadening n ^
                  2 *
                inner ℂ (data.basis m) (current₂ (data.basis n)) *
              inner ℂ (data.basis n) (current₁ (data.basis m)))

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaResidualSeaOperatorKernel
docString:
Finite-broadening residual after removing the derivative of the chosen surface primitive from
the canonical Bastin operator integrand. Keeping this remainder distinct from the conventional
Smrčka–Středa `II` term is motivated by Bonbien and Manchon, *Phys. Rev. B* **102**, 085113 (2020),
[doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.102.085113](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.102.085113), whose symmetrized
trace decomposition avoids the overlap of the conventional `I`/`II` terms. The conventional
Smrcka--Streda `I`/`II` terminology is sourced to L. Smrcka and P. Streda, *J. Phys. C* **10**,
2153 (1977), [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/10/12/021](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/10/12/021).
No direct identification of this operator remainder with the paper's trace-level sea term is
asserted here.

      SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (∃ q c,
      (∀ (i : Fin (2 * (n + 1))),
          (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C i) = Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C i) ∧
        (∀ (i j : Fin (2 * (n + 1))),
            i ≠ j → ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C i) (C j) = c i j • LinearMap.id) ∧
          ∀ (i : Fin (2 * (n + 1))), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0) →
    ∀ (j : Fin (2 * n + 1)),
      ∃ q c,
        (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)),
            (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C (j.succAbove i).succ) =
              Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C (j.succAbove i).succ) ∧
          (∀ (i j_1 : Fin (2 * n)),
              i ≠ j_1 →
                ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C (j.succAbove i).succ) (C (j.succAbove j_1).succ) =
                  c i j_1 • LinearMap.id) ∧
            ∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0

name: SecondQuantization.Common.OccupationBasis
docString:
**The occupation-basis interface**: a Fock-space basis type `Config`, together with a
`vacuum` state and a per-mode occupation-number reading `occupation : Config → Mode → ℕ`, subject
to the physically expected constraints — the vacuum has no particles anywhere, every state has
only finitely many occupied modes, and the reading determines the state. A `class` (not a plain
`structure`) so each statistics' concrete instance is found by typeclass resolution once `Mode`
and its `Config` are fixed, rather than needing to be threaded explicitly.

        ((vacuum : Config) →
            (occupation : Config → Mode → ℕ) →

                (support : Config → Finset Mode) →
                  (mem_support_iff : ∀ (n : Config) (i : Mode), i ∈ support n ↔ occupation n i ≠ 0) →
                    (ext : ∀ {m n : Config}, (∀ (i : Mode), occupation m i = occupation n i) → m = n) →
                      motive
                        { vacuum := vacuum, occupation := occupation, occupation_vacuum := occupation_vacuum,
                          support := support, mem_support_iff := mem_support_iff, ext := ext }) →

**The fiber decomposition of the diagram sum.**

The diagrams whose external component occupies exactly the interaction vertices `T` are the pairs
consisting of an externally connected two-point diagram on `T` and an arbitrary quartic diagram on
`S \ T`.  This is the statement that lets the linked-cluster factorization organize the sum over
diagrams as a Cauchy product.

The external labels come from the external piece, each vertex label is read off whichever side its
vertex belongs to, and the pairing is assembled by `Pairing.ofSplit` along `slotLegSplitting`.

not required to be externally connected. Those conditions belong to the statement that this is
inverse to the decomposition, not to the construction.

name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_operatorIntervalIntegral
docString:
**Left-composition with a fixed operator commutes with `operatorIntervalIntegral`**:
`L ∘ (∫ F) = ∫ (L ∘ F)`, given interval-integrability of every matrix coefficient `F` contributes.
Both sides reduce, via `matrixCoeff_comp`/`matrixCoeff_operatorIntervalIntegral`, to the same
`∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k * ∫ σ, matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` vs. `∫ σ, ∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k *
matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` — the finite-sum/integral interchange `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum`
supplies, after pulling the constant `matrixCoeff L m k` in/out of each summand's integral
(`intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul`). Needed to move an already-evaluated interaction-picture
vertex factor past the ordered-simplex integral over the *remaining* Dyson coefficient.

name: SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution_comp_eq_smul_comp_diagonalEvolution
docString:
**The KMS-type relation**: if a linear map `C` picks up an exponential eigenvalue-shift factor
`e^{qτ}` under `heisenbergEvolve` (as every `create`/`annihilate` operator does, with `q` the
eigenvalue shift `∓ε_i`), then `e^{τH₀}` and `C` satisfy `e^{τH₀} C = e^{qτ} C e^{τH₀}` — the exact
statistics-agnostic algebraic ingredient the finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem's
KMS-rotation step needs (`ĉ_α e^{-βĤ} = e^{-βξ_α} e^{-βĤ} ĉ_α` in the project's physics reference
notes, `quantum-statistical-mechanics.tex`'s "product-of-KMS-state-and-ladder-op"), obtained purely
by rearranging the already-proved semigroup law and mutual inversion
(`diagonalEvolution_neg_comp`) — no new physical input beyond the eigenvalue-shift hypothesis
`hC`, and in particular no dependence on the concrete occupation-state type or exchange statistics.
Both `Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` and
`Bosonic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` supply exactly this hypothesis (with
`q := -ε i`/`q := ε i` respectively), so this single `Common/` lemma gives the KMS relation for
`create`/`annihilate` in both statistics at once.

name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_eq_div_of_zetaCommutator
docString:
**The genuine normalized 2-point Bloch–de Dominicis value**: `⟨C₁Cⱼ⟩ = c₁ⱼ/(1 - ζw₁)`,
dividing the singleton-tail peel identity `(1 - ζw₁) Tr[e^{-βH₀}(C₁Cⱼ)] = c₁ⱼ Tr[e^{-βH₀}]` through
by the genuine (nonzero) partition function and by the (assumed nonzero) `1 - ζw₁` factor —
matching the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₁Ĉⱼ⟩ = C_{1,j}/(1 - ζw₁)` letter-for-letter rather than
leaving it as an un-divided trace equation.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundState_conductivity_frequency
docString:
Closed unit-volume finite-rate electrical conductivity of the unit-hopping dimer:

`σ(ω,η) = (η - iω) / ((η - iω)² + 4)`.

The proof keeps the Lehmann current response, Peierls contact `-1`, and electric-field
normalization as the existing public definitions and simplifies them only at the final scalar step.

statement:

    1 SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundStateConductivityTable =
  1 / 5
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundState_conductivity_zero_one
docString:
First exact end-to-end scalar electrical-conductivity benchmark:

`current-current = 4/5`, `contact = -1`, and the unit-volume electric-field normalization is `-1`,
so the fixed-rate conductivity at `ℏ = 1`, `ω = 0`, `η = 1` is exactly `1/5`.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue_ofSlotSplit_right_locality
docString:
The actual quartic vacuum half of an assembled external-insertion diagram has
the standalone free-Gibbs pair kernel when its vertex slots are reindexed into the
ambient diagram. The arguments retain their given order; normalization of ambient
pairs after reassembly is a separate assertion.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ) {E n : ℕ}
  (T : Finset (Fin n))
  (ext :
    SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalFieldLabel Mode)
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) E n T)
  (vac :
    SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) n (Finset.univ \ T))
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  let S := Finset.univ \ T;
  have order := (S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯).toEquiv;
  have f := fun i => ↑((S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) i);
  have d := SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.ofSlotSplit ⋯ ext vac;
  have splitting :=
    (((Equiv.refl (Fin (2 * (2 * T.card + E)))).sumCongr
              (SecondQuantization.Common.orderedLegToDiagramLeg S order)).trans
          (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionSlotLegSplitting ⋯)).trans
      (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionMixedTimeAmbientPositionEquiv externalTime σ).symm;
  have pairEquiv := Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv splitting ext.pairing (vac.pairingInOrder order);
  have kernel :=
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β d.externalLabel externalTime
      (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexLabelSequence d) σ;
  ∀ (pr : (vac.pairingInOrder order).NormalizedPair),
    kernel (↑(pairEquiv (Sum.inr pr))).1 (↑(pairEquiv (Sum.inr pr))).2 =
      if splitting (Sum.inr (↑pr).1) < splitting (Sum.inr (↑pr).2) then
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairValue ε β (fun v => vac.vertexLabel ((S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) v))
          (σ ∘ f) (↑pr).1 (↑pr).2
      else
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairValue ε β (fun v => vac.vertexLabel ((S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) v))
          (σ ∘ f) (↑pr).2 (↑pr).1

  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  let S := Finset.univ \ T;
  have order := (S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯).toEquiv;
  have f := fun i => ↑((S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) i);
  have fT := fun i => ↑((T.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) i);
  have localFixed :=
    Equiv.symm
      (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionStandardToMixedAtomicPositionEquiv externalTime
        (σ ∘ fun i => ↑((T.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) i)));
  have split :=
    (((Equiv.refl (Fin (2 * (2 * T.card + E)))).sumCongr
              (SecondQuantization.Common.orderedLegToDiagramLeg S order)).trans
          (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionSlotLegSplitting ⋯)).trans
      (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionMixedTimeAmbientPositionEquiv externalTime σ).symm;
  have mixedSplit := (localFixed.sumCongr (Equiv.refl (Fin (2 * (2 * S.card))))).trans split;
  have localPairing := Combinatorics.PairingOn.transport ext.pairing localFixed;
  have d := SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.ofSlotSplit ⋯ ext vac;
  have kernel :=
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β d.externalLabel externalTime
      (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexLabelSequence d) σ;
  have leftKernel :=
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β ext.externalLabel externalTime
      (fun v => ext.vertexLabel ((T.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) v)) (σ ∘ fT);
  have rightKernel :=
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairValue ε β (fun v => vac.vertexLabel ((S.orderIsoOfFin ⋯) v)) (σ ∘ f);
  StrictAnti (σ ∘ f) →
    (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime σ).evaluation
        (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion
          (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime σ))
        kernel =
      (↑SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion.zetaInt ^
          ∑ i, ∑ j, if mixedSplit (Sum.inr j) < mixedSplit (Sum.inl i) then 1 else 0) *

docString:
The actual physical mixed-time pairing evaluation splits into its standalone
external-support and ordered-vacuum evaluations, up to the fermionic sign of
the right-before-left inter-sector positions. The external pairing is first
transported into its own mixed-time atomic order; the vacuum vertices are in
a strictly antitone chamber. Neither kernel is assumed symmetric under
reversal of the pair endpoints.
